narrative.overview: ClassVault's surfaces behave like the institutional ledger where things are recorded, stamped, and verified — the physical object that makes trust legible. Deep bottle-green fields ruled with faint ledger lines carry the brand's authority (the quiet of a library desk lamp at 11pm, not a startup pitch); true-neutral off-white pages carry the reading. Verification isn't asserted in copy — it's stamped, in marigold ink, slightly rotated, textured like a real rubber stamp. Notes appear as numbered register entries with inked star ratings.
keyCharacteristics: Committed color: bottle green carries ~40-50% of the page; marigold is the only accent
Young Serif display — chunky 1970s-schoolbook warmth, one weight, never bolded
The rubber stamp as the brand's autograph for verification states
Ledger grammar: ruled lines, entry numbers, register tables, index tabs
Honest voice: mechanics shown as proof; no fabricated numbers anywhere

rules.name: The Certifying Ink Rule
rules.body: Marigold means something was verified, rated, or is the primary action. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Two Fields Rule
rules.body: Every section sits on bottle green or off-white/white. No third background, no tints-as-sections, no gradients.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Young Serif ships only 400. Hierarchy comes from size and color; never synthesize bold or italic on the serif.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Sections open with the headline itself. Uppercase labels live inside artifacts (ledger headers, tabs, stamps), never floated above headings.

rules.name: The Printed Matter Rule
rules.body: If an element could plausibly be printed in a ledger, it gets no shadow. Shadows are reserved for the few true cards.

dos: Do commit to the green: hero, rooms, final CTA, and footer sit on Bottle Green (#0c2b21).
Do reserve marigold for trust claims and primary actions.
Do keep running text at Ink Body (#363c38) on light and Ivory-muted (72%) on green.
Do mark every product mockup 'Product preview — sample data'; sample numbers never become page claims.
Do ship a prefers-reduced-motion alternative for every animation, including the stamp entrance.
donts: Don't build "generic SaaS landing" furniture: gradient heroes, hero-metric stat rows, identical icon-heading-text card grids.
Don't use "ed-tech cliché" imagery: graduation caps, chalkboards, childlike primary-color play.
Don't add "social/engagement app" mechanics: streaks, likes, FOMO countdowns, fake urgency.
Don't drift into "sterile note tool" gray minimalism.
Don't fabricate proof: no invented user counts, university totals, partner marquees, or aspirational stats anywhere.
Don't revert to the cream/paper editorial-serif lane (Instrument Serif, mono eyebrows, tape/stickers).
Don't use gradient text, side-stripe borders, glassmorphism, or repeated uppercase eyebrows above headings.
Don't put a stamp on anything that isn't a verification, status, or certification moment.
